'''Yuri Dolgorukiy''' (Юрий Долгорукий, "Yuri the Long-Armed"; c. 1090s – 15 May 1157), Yuri I Vladimirovich, was a Rurikid prince of Rostov-Suzdal and Grand Prince of Kiev.

He was a son of [[Vladimir II Monomakh]]. He held Kiev twice, in 1149–1151 and from 1155 until his death there in 1157.

He is traditionally regarded as the founder of [[Moscow]]. Its first mention in the chronicles is in 1147, as the place where Yuri hosted Sviatoslav Olgovich. He also founded Pereslavl-Zalessky, Yuryev-Polsky and Dmitrov.

His sons included [[Andrey Bogolyubsky]] and [[Vsevolod the Big Nest]].
